title: Hyderabad
thought: This feels exciting. Maybe VLSI is the thing I will do forever.
story: I started with Electronics and VLSI because I genuinely liked understanding what was happening under the surface. Then COVID slowed everything down, and I started exploring coding just for fun. I was a complete beginner, but making something work on my own felt exciting.

title: COVID Sandbox
thought: Wait... coding is actually fun. Is this just a phase? Let me keep going.
story: I did not have a perfect plan. I watched YouTube, searched Google, took Coursera courses, and tried whatever looked interesting. I was simply learning what kind of work kept me curious.

title: Mysuru
thought: Maybe this is what I want to do forever... let me see how far I can take it.
story: Mysuru was my first time living away from home. I was nervous, excited, and honestly ready to learn everything. Infosys training gave structure to my curiosity through Java, Selenium, SQL, testing, and the complete software process.

title: Chennai
thought: Okay, maybe this is the real career path. Or maybe I am still figuring it out.
story: In Chennai, the work became real. I was validating banking systems, tracking defects, checking ETL transformations, and understanding why something failed instead of only marking it as failed. Being promoted to Test Engineer showed me how much I enjoyed investigation.

title: The Leap
thought: Will I really pull this off? I guess there is only one way to find out.
story: I knew in my gut that I wanted work that kept changing and challenging me. Data felt right because every problem looked different. Moving abroad as a first-generation student was a huge step, but my excitement to learn was stronger than the fear.

title: Northeastern
thought: This finally feels like all the pieces are connecting. Maybe this is it.
story: Northeastern changed how I looked at analytics. SQL, machine learning, dashboards, forecasting, and AI stopped feeling like separate subjects. They became one process: understand the question, validate the data, build the solution, and explain what it means.

title: Nexodus Inc.
thought: This is the first time my work clearly saved people time. I want more of this.
story: At Nexodus, I saw how much time people were losing to repetitive reporting. I automated collection, worked on Power BI dashboards, and helped retain historical data. Cutting reporting time by 70% taught me that useful analytics should make someone’s day easier.

title: Nexodus Inc.
thought: So AI is not just about models. Trust comes first. That changed everything.
story: In my co-op, I worked with messy source data and unstructured social content. I caught recurring issues before reporting and built a BERT pipeline. The biggest lesson was simple: people trust the result only when the data behind it is clean and explainable.

title: Graduation
thought: Maybe this is the end of one trail... but definitely not the end of the journey.
story: Graduating with a 3.9 GPA still feels surreal. I moved from electronics to coding, testing, analytics, an internship, a co-op, and finally a master’s in Analytics with a Machine Intelligence concentration.

title: Living Stones
thought: I still do not know exactly how far this trail goes. That is the fun part.
story: Now I am a Geospatial Analyst at Living Stones Foundation, ranking water risk for all 184 municipalities in Ceará, Brazil. I am working where analytics, engineering, and AI meet. I do not want to build models only because I can. I want to build systems that help people understand what is happening, why it matters, and what to do next.
